data.title: Invoicing: AS-38 review follow-ups (T1 tautology, stale health test name, ';' body separator, /healthz config exposure)

data.to:
Four non-blocking findings from the AS-38 QA review (qa-priya, review comment 2026-09-02T00:45Z; items B.4-B.7), bundled because each is a one-line-to-one-function change in apps/invoicing and none changes behaviour visible to a user. AS-38 merged at 66b9fb9.

1. test/stripe-client.test.js:625 — T1 carries a tautological assertion: `!(x in h) || h[x] !== undefined` is always true, so it pins nothing. Either pin the intended property (`'user-agent' not in unsigned.headers` — the transport sends no User-Agent of its own) or delete the line. Decide which the test MEANT; do not just make it pass.

2. test/health.test.js:61 — test name 'no secrets exist yet, so redacted() equals the config' is stale wording since AS-38 introduced the first secret-shaped setting (INVOICING_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY). The assertion still holds because the key is unset in tests. Rename to say what it now checks (an unconfigured secret redacts to null and the rest of the config is unchanged). Flagged independently by both the implementer and the reviewer.

3. lib/stripe/custody.js — guard hardening: a raw `;`-separated body (`customer=cus_1;transfer_data[destination]=acct_x`) passes guardRequest because URLSearchParams splits only on `&`. Unreachable in v1: encodeForm percent-encodes `;` and only client.js may import transport.js (dependency-policy M5b). Fix options, pick one and add the test that fails without it: reject a raw `;` in any body the guard sees, or split on the same separator set Stripe accepts. Keep "values are never inspected" (plan §2).

4. lib/health.js / routes/health.js — /healthz publishes the redacted config object (pre-existing AS-37 behaviour, not an AS-38 criterion). Redaction is proven (AS-38 AC 4, test/health.test.js 'the health body carries redacted config, never raw config'), but a public health endpoint that enumerates setting names and non-secret values (bind, port, env) is more than a health check needs. Decide: drop the config object from /healthz, or gate it behind INVOICING_ENV !== 'production'. Must land before anything is publicly reachable; not urgent while the app runs on loopback only.

Acceptance: each item has a test that fails without the change (house technique — show the checker red once, record the failing-test set); the suite stays 8 files; dependency-policy, deploy-shape and harness guards stay green; no new dependencies; no protected top-level files touched. Complexity low. Plan can be short.

data.body: Filed from Priya's AS-38 review (findings B.4–B.7). Bundled: four one-liners in apps/invoicing, none user-visible. Item 4 (/healthz config exposure) is the only one with a deadline — before anything is publicly reachable.
